title: Exploring Interpretability for Visual Prompt Tuning with Cross-layer Concepts
claim: Interpretable prompts come from category-agnostic concept prototypes that discover regions and aggregate features at every layer, then fuse fine-to-coarse.
layout: 2 panels: layer-wise stack left (bottom-to-top), module detail right in blue box
description: A two-part architecture diagram. On the left, three frozen Transformer layers (snowflake icons) are stacked bottom to top, with a classifier at the top. At each layer, learnable concept prototypes (flame icons, green boxes) feed a 'D' node (Concept Region Discovery). That node produces concept-level attention maps, shown as stacked bird images with heatmaps. An 'A' node (Intra-region Feature Aggregation) turns the maps into colored prompt-embedding bars. Fusion layers, guided by coarse-grained bird region images, merge the prompts from fine to coarse. A dotted box labeled 'Decrease' shows the number of prototypes shrinking with depth. On the right, a light-blue panel details the CRD and IFA modules. Patch embeddings and prototypes go through similarity, softmax and bias injection, then argmax masking. Region grouping then produces prompt embeddings. Pastel colors show the data flow.
caption: IVPT introduces category-agnostic concept prototypes to generate explainable visual prompt embeddings. At each layer, Concept Region Discovery (CRD) module captures specific visual concepts as concept-level image regions, while Intra-region Feature Aggregation (IFA) module aggregates features grouped by these region maps to obtain prompt embeddings. Several sets of layer-wise concept prototypes are used to capture concepts across layers, while the fusion layer, guided by the coarse-grained region, fuses the prompts in a fine-to-coarse manner as the final prompts to replace flat visual prompts at each layer.
abstract: Visual prompt tuning offers significant advantages for adapting pre-trained visual foundation models to specific tasks. However, current research provides limited insight into the interpretability of this approach, which is essential for enhancing AI reliability and enabling AI-driven knowledge discovery. In this paper, rather than learning abstract prompt embeddings, we propose the first framework, named Interpretable Visual Prompt Tuning (IVPT), to explore interpretability for visual prompts by introducing cross-layer concept prototypes. Specifically, visual prompts are linked to human-understandable semantic concepts, represented as a set of category-agnostic prototypes, each corresponding to a specific region of the image. IVPT then aggregates features from these regions to generate interpretable prompts for multiple network layers, allowing the explanation of visual prompts at different network depths and semantic granularities. Comprehensive qualitative and quantitative evaluations on fine-grained classification benchmarks show its superior interpretability and performance over visual prompt tuning methods and existing interpretable methods.
